dataset_family: cogSYS user-study-1 sample, Beijing (National Research Center for Rehabilitation Technical Aids / ICT-CAS), n=61 (20 'MCI' / 41 controls); self-collected, non-public
method_family: Touchscreen drag-and-drop hand-motor kinematics under single/dual-task paradigm (plus ASR counts in dual tasks); iterative random-forest feature selection + SMOTE random forest; LOOCV repeated 100 times; majority vote across tasks
what_it_shows: A one-minute drag-and-drop test on a consumer Huawei M5 tablet, performed 'independently' in a lab with experimenters present, separates 20 'MCI' participants from 41 controls. Best single-task accuracy is 89.5%; majority voting over all seven tasks gives 90.1%; the mean over tasks is 82.4% (LOOCV repeated 100 times). The 'MCI' label is disjunctive: MoCA < 25 OR APOE e4. Controls have no cognitive screening score reported. No head-to-head against a specialist instrument.
why: Zhang et al. 2021 (Int J Human-Computer Studies 145:102547). The PDF title, authors and DOI match the block and the map entry. What fits: (1) Consumer device: the classifier data come from a Huawei M5 Android tablet (p.8). (2) High best-case standalone accuracy: T2 89.5%, V2 90.1% (Table 3, p.10; Section 7.2, p.15), inside ~88-94%. (3) Small internally validated sample, no external validation, and no head-to-head: the user-experience study compares questionnaire ratings of BBT/DBBT/66nao, not accuracy. What only partly fits. (a) Self-administration: experimenters explained the procedure and were present throughout. The paper says they 'cannot interfere' and that subjects finish the tasks 'independently' (p.8). But all three studies ran in a lab with an experimenter present, and independent use is argued, not tested (p.15-16). (b) The reference standard: the positive class is 'MoCA scores lower than 25 or an Apolipoprotein E gene type of e4' (p.7). APOE genotype alone is not cognitive impairment, and 70% of the group are e4 carriers with mean MoCA 22.88 (SD 3.55) (Table 2, p.8). So some 'MCI' cases may qualify on genotype alone. Controls are described only as 'without any sign of cognitive decline' and no MoCA is printed for them. This is a weaker reference than P-101's MoCA-defined proxy, because part of the label is non-cognitive. The reported accuracy is therefore accuracy against a MoCA-or-APOE label, not against MCI or a cognitive proxy alone. That is why I answer 'partly' on the narrowed wording too. If the operator accepts a named proxy label, as round 20 did for P-101, the device, accuracy and validation strands of the narrowed wording fit, and the proxy would have to be named as 'MoCA<25 or APOE e4'. Other caveats. The headline in the abstract and contributions is the mean 82.4%. Single tasks T1/T3 give 73.4%/75.4%, which the authors call 'only slightly better than ... random guess'. The method was chosen because it was 'obviously superior' to DT/SVM/kNN on the same data, and only its results are reported. The paper does not state whether feature selection and SMOTE ran inside the LOOCV folds. Independence: Beijing, ICT-CAS and NRCRTA authors (Zhang, Chen, Yu, Lv, Yang, Hu, Zhang). No overlap with P-101's Shanghai Jiao Tong authors or its Shanghai/Henan sample, none with I-CONECT (P-76/P-77), none with the other candidates.

quotes.quote: The MCI group consisted of 20 subjects selected by the MoCA scale and the Apolipoprotein E genetic test. The "drag & drop" prototype was run on a Huawei M5 tablet (Android 8.0, 4GB/64GB, with a 10.1-inch, 1920 × 1200 pixels touchscreen). The experiment was conducted in the presence of experimenters whose main job was to clarify the experimental rules and procedures and observe the subjects' performance. They cannot interfere with the specific process, and the subjects should finish the seven "drag & drop" tasks independently.

We leveraged the leave-one-out cross validation to validate the effectiveness of our method. Specifically, the data of one subject was used as the test data set, and the data of the remaining 60 subjects were used as the training data set. In addition, we repeated this leave-one-out cross validation process 100 times

Single-task II achieved the best detection accuracy of 89.5%. ... In contrast, the classification results of single-tasks I and III were the worst in all four metrics. Their classification accuracies were 73.4% and 75.4% respectively, which were only slightly better than that of random guess.

Experimental results show that the detection accuracy of our classification method is obviously superior to traditional machine learning methods, such as decision tree, support vector machine, and k-nearest neighbor. Thus, we only report the technical details and classification results of our method
Regarding the cognitive assessment results, a mean accuracy of 82.4% and a maximum accuracy of 90.1% were achieved

three user studies were all conducted in laboratory environment with the participant of experimenter. Though the feasibility of the independent usage of "drag & drop" is demonstrated in Section 7.1, home environment-based experiments are still necessary
